title: Quick-Fix: Add Unit for Undeclared at Cursor (Ctrl+Alt+U)
summary: Finds which unit declares the identifier under the caret and adds that unit to the current unit's uses clause
intro: Read this when the compiler would report an undeclared identifier. Put the caret on it (Ctrl+Alt+U) and drag-lint finds the unit that declares it and adds that unit to your uses clause.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Quick-Fix: Add Unit for Undeclared at Cursor (Ctrl+Alt+U)
steps: Put the caret on the undeclared identifier in the editor
Press Ctrl+Alt+U, or choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Quick-Fix: Add Unit for Undeclared at Cursor (Ctrl+Alt+U)
The unit that declares the identifier is added to the current unit's uses clause

questions.ask: The compiler says an identifier is undeclared; which unit declares it?
questions.command: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Quick-Fix: Add Unit for Undeclared at Cursor (Ctrl+Alt+U)

questions.ask: How do I add the missing unit to uses without typing it?
questions.command: Ctrl+Alt+U with the caret on the identifier
